course_name_original: Análisis y Recuperación de Información Textual
prerequisites: Knowledge of machine learning (I and II)

learning_outcomes.text: Know the main natural language processing techniques.
Apply NLP techniques for text categorization and sentiment analysis.
Know how to represent a social network in graph format.
Know the main techniques and methods for analyzing the structure and content of social networks.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to text processing: Character encoding standards and fundamentals of working with digital texts and corpora.
Formal languages and regular expressions: Deterministic finite automata and use of regular expressions for identifying and extracting patterns in text.
Text extraction and processing from documents: Obtaining text from document formats such as PDF and designing software for scalable processing of heterogeneous corpora from variable sources.
Lexical analysis and classical preprocessing: Tokenization, normalization, lemmatization, stemming, and other techniques for preparing corpora for analysis.
Vector representation of texts: Classic representation models (bag-of-words, TF, TF-IDF) and introduction to embeddings.

Use cases of language models: Use of pre-trained language models for various natural language processing tasks. Application of vector representations to text classification tasks and automatic entity detection, among other token classification tasks.
Adaptation of language models and conversational systems: Fine-tuning pre-trained models for specific tasks and development of conversational systems based on language models.
Information retrieval: Retrieval models based on indices and textual information, evaluation using standard metrics, and development of applications based on corpus search.
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): Integration of language models with information retrieval systems to build question-answering systems over document corpora.
Network and graph analysis: Construction of graphs from textual data, similarity measures, and community detection.
teaching_methods: Online asynchronous learning (videos, virtual campus activities, recommended readings, solved examples)

assessment_methods.method: Participation in seminars and online or in-person continuous assessment activities
Theory evaluation (EVT) - weighted average of three independent blocks

assessment_rules: The final grade is 0.15*PA + 0.425*EVT + 0.425*EVP. To pass, the individual grade for each theory and practice evaluation must be greater than or equal to 4 out of 10. If any individual evaluation does not meet this minimum, the final grade will be min(4, 0.15*PA + 0.425*EVT + 0.425*EVP). In extraordinary calls, the same weightings and minimums apply.
